claims.text: The starting material is a cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical lamellar microstructure containing soft FCC and hard B2 phases.
Dislocations accumulate near internal phase boundaries in the untreated alloy.
Boundary-associated dislocation pile-ups promote microcrack nucleation and limited ductility.
Phase-selective annealing can fully recrystallize the soft FCC phase while retaining a hard B2 skeleton.
Annealing at about 700 °C can produce the proposed phase-selective recrystallization.
The treatment can preserve the integrity and spacing of the B2 phase without coarsening it.
Phase-selective recrystallization produces a fully recrystallized soft phase embedded in a retained hard phase.
The recrystallized FCC domains have modified, less aggressive boundaries that reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Recrystallization lowers the local dislocation density at FCC/B2 boundaries.
Reducing boundary pile-ups minimizes local stress concentrations and delays localized cracking.
Strong semi-coherent boundaries between the FCC and hard ordered BCC/B2 phase promote dislocation storage and work hardening in the FCC phase.
Retaining the hard phase and effective phase boundaries preserves or enhances overall strength.
The treated alloy can achieve approximately 35% uniform elongation.
Uniform elongation will increase from a typical untreated value of about 25% to approximately 35%.
The treated alloy will maintain or slightly increase its yield strength.
The treated alloy's yield strength will be approximately 0.94–2 GPa.
The untreated alloy exhibits brittle behavior at room temperature.
Over-annealing can cause grain growth or boundary coarsening that exacerbates dislocation pile-ups and negates the improvements.
The optimal annealing temperature and time depend sensitively on alloy composition and initial microstructure.

contradictions.description: The untreated alloy is characterized as brittle, yet the predicted comparison assigns it about 25% uniform elongation, which is substantial tensile ductility and is difficult to reconcile with an unqualified brittle baseline.

The mediator attributes improvement to modified, less aggressive phase boundaries, whereas the mechanism attributes continued strengthening to retained strong semi-coherent boundaries; the hypothesis does not clarify which boundary attributes change and which remain intact.
